**Tier G** — governance — identity, capability, delegation, audit · owned by `platform` · `public.user_ai_permissions`

**One row is** One user's AI entitlements — which models they may reach, which one they get by default, and how the request is shaped. One row per user, or none.

The empty-array-means-everything rule in `allowed_model_ids` is the one thing a reader of this table must not get wrong. It is deliberate — it preserves the pre-column behaviour for every user who has no row — but it inverts the usual reading of an allow-list, and nothing at the point of display says so (§5 T2).

| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |

| Policies on the table | 2 — all carry a predicate |

Read by `capabilities_for_user()` into the `models` block of its result, which is what the chat surfaces use to decide what to offer. Not part of the four capability layers — a capability answers "may you", this answers "with what".

**Substitutions** — every point where a value you did not supply can stand in
for one you did.

| When | The value used | Shown as | Visible where |
|---|---|---|---|
| the array is empty, or the user has no row at all | every enabled model is allowed | `default` | nowhere, and it is worth stating plainly: EMPTY MEANS EVERYTHING here, not nothing. The resolver sets `all_allowed` true when the array is empty or absent, which preserves the behaviour that existed before the column did. An administrator clearing the list to revoke access would grant all of it instead. |
